ns1:channel.ns1:title: Nature Sustainability
ns1:channel.ns1:description: Nature Sustainability will publish significant original research from a broad range of natural, social and engineering fields about sustainability, its policy dimensions and possible solutions. Understanding how to ensure the well-being of current and future generations within the limits of the natural world is the overarching goal of sustainability research. Nature Sustainability will cover topics including water, air and soil pollution, agriculture and food security, water–energy–land nexus, water-soil-waste nexus and climate change, among many others.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Urban energy and transport impacts of autonomous robotaxi deployment
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01944-2

Autonomous robotaxis are being used in certain urban transport systems, but how they affect fleets and energy use is underexplored. A study now shows that robotaxis overlap with taxi demand but complement public transit, and optimized deployment could cut fleet size by 62.5% and energy use by 44.8%.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Sequential electronic reconstruction enables durable oxygen redox in water electrolysis
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01940-6

Electrocatalytic water oxidation remains a bottleneck for green hydrogen production due to efficiency limits. Here the authors show a sequential reconstruction activation strategy that overcomes these issues by decoupling oxygen-redox activity from lattice instability, enabling exciting performance.
